title: Region-aware placement policies and deterministic failover for Dedicated fleets
creator: Priya Raman
description:
Problem: Customers using Dedicated capacity require deterministic control over where their fleet runs (region and zone), strict data residency guarantees, and predictable throughput during zone outages or cloud failures. Current scheduler routes by cheapest-available capacity which can violate residency constraints or cause unexpected cold-fallback to distant regions, leading to latency and compliance issues.

Goal: Implement a region-aware placement and failover model for Dedicated fleets that: 1) enforces customer-configured residency constraints, 2) provides clear placement strategy primitives (strict zonal, regional preferred, cross-region fallback with policy), and 3) integrates with autoscaling to preserve throughput guarantees during partial failures while honoring residency. This ticket covers the control-plane config surface, scheduler/controller changes, routing fallback semantics, and a rollout plan with observability and safety gates.
acceptance_criteria: API: Fleet config accepts a placement_policy enum and residency tag; new schema validated by control-plane and accepted by UI
Behavior: For a fleet with 'regional_strict' residency, no nodes in other regions will be selected during normal operations or automated failover

Failover: In-zone failure triggers deterministic fallback defined by policy: either 'fail' (stop accepting new traffic), 'regional-degrade' (shift traffic to other zones in same region), or 'cross-region-cooldown' (allow cross-region only after operator-approved cooldown), and behavior is logged
Autoscaling: Scale-up/scale-down decisions maintain throughput SLOs under normal load and during regional failures up to configured burst capacity
Metrics: Dashboards show per-fleet placement decisions, failover events, and per-region throughput; alerts fire for unexpected cross-region placements
Security & Compliance: Residency configuration is audit-logged and surfaced in tenant audit logs
Migration: Existing Dedicated fleets without placement_policy default to current behavior but opt-in path exists and documented
implementation_steps: Control-plane: extend fleet API schema with 'placement_policy' and 'residency_constraint' fields and server-side validation
Scheduler: add region-aware placement algorithm with pre-filter for residency; implement scoring to prefer same-zone, then same-region, then allowed cross-region based on policy
Routing: update frontend routing to prefer local endpoints and respect strict flags to reject cross-region routing requests
Autoscaler: introduce placement-aware scaling decisions that can allocate burst_capacity in-region and track per-zone headroom
Fallback controller: implement deterministic failover state machine with explicit cooldown and operator override hooks
Observability: emit placement_decision, failover_reason, residency_violation, and cross_region_usage metrics; add logs in audit stream
UI/CLI: add fleet configuration UX for placement_policy and residency, with inline validation and migration helper
E2E tests: simulate zone failure, quota shortage, and verify behavior for all policies
Runbook: update incident runbooks to include new failover states and rollback procedures
testing_and_rollout: Stage 1 (internal): deploy control-plane changes to staging and create test fleets with each placement policy; validate non-breaking behavior for default fleets
Stage 2 (canary): enable placement_policy opt-in for 5% of new Dedicated fleets in prod; monitor metrics and error budgets for 48 hours
Stage 3 (customer pilots): invite two enterprise customers with residency requirements to pilot and provide feedback
Stage 4 (gradual): increase opt-in surface to 50% then 100% with automated migration tool for existing fleets
Safety gates: block rollout if cross_region_usage > 0.5% for regional_strict fleets or if error rate increases > 2x baseline
metrics_and_dashboards: residency_violation_alert (firing if any regional_strict fleet has >0 cross-region requests in 10m)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Strict residency may cause capacity shortages and request rejections. Mitigation: provide clear UX to set min_capacity and burst_capacity; autoscaler reserves in-region headroom
Risk: Cross-region fallback increases latency and potentially breaks compliance. Mitigation: require explicit policy opt-in for cross-region fallback and operator approvals for cooldown windows
Risk: Scheduler complexity increases leading to regressions. Mitigation: keep pre-filter + score separation, add unit and property tests, and a canary rollout
Risk: Customers will be confused about default behavior. Mitigation: default to current behavior for existing fleets and require explicit configuration for strict residency
notes: Design trade-offs considered: 1) enforcing hard residency in allocator vs rejecting out-of-region routing at gateway; we chose allocator enforcement + gateway guardrails for defense in depth
We considered a proactive capacity reservation market but deferred to autoscaler headroom to keep initial scope small
This work pairs with PM signage and Console UX owned by PM-5821 for policy exposition and compliance reports
